content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

# My Books

A tiny reading tracker. No accounts, no database — books live in `data/books.json`.

```sh
npm start        # http://127.0.0.1:3000
npm test
```

- The home page lists what you're currently reading and what you've finished, with a form to add a book.
- Each book has its own page (`/books/<id>`) showing title, author and notes, with a copyable share link.
- From a book's page you can mark it finished or update your notes.

Configuration (all optional): `PORT` (default `3000`), `HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`; use `0.0.0.0` to share links with other devices on your network), `BOOKS_FILE` (default `data/books.json`).

content.text:
The app is built and working. Run it with `npm start` and open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

## What you get

- **Home page** (`/`): two lists, "Currently reading" and "Finished" (newest first), plus an add-a-book form with title, author and notes. Empty states show a friendly message.
- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`): title, author, status with date, your notes, a "Mark as finished" button (hidden once finished), and a read-only "Share link" box that selects itself on click. The link is the plain URL of that page, so you can just send it to someone.
- **Persistence**: books are saved to `data/books.json` (pretty-printed, easy to hand-edit). Writes go to a temp file then rename, so a crash mid-save can't corrupt your data. I verified this by adding two books, finishing one, killing the server, restarting, and confirming both lists came back correctly.

One small addition beyond your list: the notes on the book page are editable with a "Save notes" button, since notes about a book tend to change while you're reading it. It's one extra route; easy to remove if you don't want it.

## How it's built

Zero runtime dependencies — just Node's built-in `http` module and server-rendered HTML, which fits "nothing fancy" and keeps it easy to read:

- `src/store.js` — reads/writes the JSON file (`list`, `get`, `add`, `finish`, `setNotes`), validates that title and author are present.
- `src/server.js` — routes: `GET /`, `POST /books`, `GET /books/:id`, `POST /books/:id/finish`, `POST /books/:id/notes`.
- `src/html.js` — page templates, with all user input HTML-escaped.
- `index.js` — entry point; `PORT`, `HOST` and `BOOKS_FILE` env vars are optional overrides.

`npm test` runs 15 vitest tests (all passing) covering the store's persistence and the HTTP flows: adding, validation errors, finishing, notes, escaping, and 404s.

`data/` is gitignored so your reading list doesn't end up committed. Nothing has been committed — the new files are in your working tree for you to review.
